name: Trash Can Robot
shortDescription: Mobile trash can on a differential-drive base: ESP32-S3 camera + motor firmware, ROS 2 nodes on a Mac, and a parametric OpenSCAD chassis.
description:
A trash can that drives itself around. The robot is a cutting-board base with two 12 V DC motors, a printed rear swivel caster and 3D-printed mounts, all generated from a parametric OpenSCAD model. An ESP32-S3 (OV3660 camera, L298N H-bridge) streams MJPEG video over HTTP and takes motor commands over UDP; inference and control run in a ROS 2 Humble stack on a MacBook Air.

Highlights:
- ESP32-S3 firmware (PlatformIO): MJPEG camera stream, JSON motor commands on UDP:4210, mDNS (`trashcam.local`), a `/health` endpoint and a once-a-second UDP heartbeat, plus serial test commands (`MOTOR`, `STOP`, `SCAN`, `CAPTURE`).
- Failsafes at both ends: the firmware stops the motors if no command arrives for 300 ms and reboots on long WiFi outages or repeated camera failures; a ROS 2 `safety_monitor_node` clamps speeds and publishes zero when `/cmd_vel` goes stale or the heartbeat drops.
- ROS 2 nodes for camera, motors, safety and keyboard teleop, with a Foxglove Studio layout for visualization.
- Parametric OpenSCAD CAD (`cad/robot.scad`) for every printed part: motor brackets, camera cradle, caster, electronics mounts and the can tabs, rendered and exported to STL by a script.
